content.text: Questions & answersWhich NBA games can I watch on Prime Video?Prime members can watch NBA on Prime games throughout the regular season for no additional fees, including the semifinals and championship games of the Emirates NBA Cup, plus every game of the SoFi Play-In Tournament and select playoff games. Additional NBA games are available via add-on subscriptions to NBA League Pass, Peacock, or Fox Sports One.How can I find NBA games on Prime Video?To find NBA games, go to the Prime Video app on your TV, computer, or mobile device, and you’ll see games on your homepage in Sports carousels, the Sports page, or the NBA League page. You can also search NBA, team names, or a specific game.On which devices can I watch NBA games on Prime Video?NBA games are available on Amazon devices such as the Fire TV and Fire tablet, connected TVs, web browsers, and on more than 650 connected devices via the Prime Video app. Click here to see the full list of supported devices.Can I record, fast forward, and rewind NBA games on Prime Video?Rewind, pause and fast forward functions are available for Android/iOS Mobile, Web (Chrome, Firefox, Edge), Fire TV, Apple TV (Gen 3 and latest) and select Smart TVs.I still need help watching NBA games on Prime Video.If you see "this video is unavailable" or "unavailable due to regional restrictions" that means the game isn't available in your area due to regional or national broadcast rights for that specific game. If you see "enable location for event availability" on mobile devices, location services might be turned off. To fix this, go to your device's settings and turn on location services for Prime Video. If you have anti-virus software, make sure it doesn't block Prime Video from accessing location services. If you see "Home region verification required", please sign in to Prime Video using a device in your home region to verify your location and continue streaming.See more questions and answers
